description: Replace CPS suspension system with unified state machine architecture — zero per-suspension heap allocations for yield, await, parallel, and race

userStories.title: Suspension point analysis pass
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to walk the AST of a suspending function, identify all suspension points (yield/await/parallel/race), and number them sequentially, so the state machine code generator knows how many resume points exist and where they are.
acceptanceCriteria: New function compiler__analyze_suspensions in compiler.c walks AST recursively
Detects yield, await, parallel, and race nodes at any nesting depth (inside if/while/for)
Assigns sequential integer IDs (0, 1, 2, ...) to each suspension point
Records the AST node, suspension type (yield/await/parallel/race), and source location per point
Nested closures/lambdas are NOT analyzed as part of the parent — they get their own analysis if they suspend
Functions with zero suspension points are not flagged for state machine compilation
Result stored in a SuspensionAnalysis struct with suspension_count, suspension_points array
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra

userStories.title: Local classification and StateLayout struct
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to classify which locals must live in the state object and produce a StateLayout struct, so the code generator can emit state-field access for those variables.
acceptanceCriteria: Conservative strategy: ALL locals in a suspending function are placed in the state object
Parameters are included in the state layout (they must survive across suspension points)
Each local gets a sequential field index in the state object
Mutable locals (mut) are tracked with an is_mutable flag on the field entry
Result is a StateLayout struct: field_count, field names (for debug), field-to-local index mapping
StateLayout is produced by compiler__analyze_suspensions alongside suspension point data
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra

userStories.title: OBJ_STATE_MACHINE GC object type
userStories.description: As the runtime, I need a new GC-managed object type that holds a state machine's local fields, resume point, error handler, and SM closure reference, so state machines have a heap-allocated home for persistent state.
acceptanceCriteria: New object kind OBJ_STATE_MACHINE added to GC object type enum in gc.c
Struct layout: uint32_t resume_point, uint32_t field_count, JaclVal error_k, JaclVal sm_closure, JaclVal fields[] (trailing array)
sm_closure field holds the compiled state machine function (a JaclClosure with the bytecode)
Allocation function gc_alloc_state_machine(heap, field_count) allocates object + trailing field array in one allocation
All fields initialized to JACL_NIL on allocation, resume_point initialized to 0
GC tracing in gc_collect.c: traces error_k, sm_closure, and all fields[0..field_count-1]
GC sweep handles OBJ_STATE_MACHINE (same as other variable-size objects)
Helper macros: jacl_is_state_machine(val), jacl_as_state_machine(val), jacl_state_machine(ptr)
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra

userStories.title: OP_GET_STATE_FIELD and OP_SET_STATE_FIELD opcodes
userStories.description: As the VM, I need opcodes to read and write fields on the current state machine object, so compiled state machine bodies can access their locals through the state object instead of stack-relative addressing.
acceptanceCriteria: OP_GET_STATE_FIELD added to OpCode enum in bytecode.c — operand: uint8_t field index
OP_SET_STATE_FIELD added to OpCode enum in bytecode.c — operand: uint8_t field index
VM handler for OP_GET_STATE_FIELD: reads state machine object from frame stack_base + 0, reads fields[index], pushes onto stack
VM handler for OP_SET_STATE_FIELD: reads state machine object from frame stack_base + 0, pops value from stack, writes to fields[index]
Opcode names registered in opcode_names[] debug table in bytecode.c
Update test/test_bytecode.c opcode enum test for new opcode count
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra

userStories.title: Compiler flag for state machine vs CPS
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a compiler flag to choose between state machine and CPS compilation for suspending functions, so both paths can coexist during the migration.
acceptanceCriteria: New field bool use_state_machines on the Compiler struct, default false
When true, suspending functions will use the state machine path (once implemented in later stories)
When false, existing CPS path is used unchanged
Flag propagated to nested compilers (continuation compilers, parallel body compilers) via compiler__init or enclosing pointer
All existing tests pass with flag set to false (no behavior change)
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra

userStories.title: State machine dispatch table emission
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to emit a dispatch table at the entry of state machine functions that jumps to the correct resume point based on state->resume_point, so resumed execution lands at the right code position.
acceptanceCriteria: New compiler helper compiler__emit_sm_dispatch_table that emits the entry dispatch for a state machine function
Loads resume_point from state object (OP_GET_STATE_FIELD on the resume_point field or a dedicated mechanism)
Emits chained conditional jumps: compare resume_point against each known ID, jump to the corresponding label
Jump targets are backpatched after body compilation (reuse existing backpatching from if/while)
Case 0 (initial entry) falls through to the function body start
Labels for each resume point stored in an array for backpatching during body emission
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: The dispatch table references labels emitted later during body compilation. Use forward-jump placeholders that get backpatched, same pattern as existing if/while compilation.

userStories.title: State machine codegen for generator body (basic yield)
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to compile a generator body into state machine bytecode when use_state_machines is true, handling basic yield (no nested control flow yet), so simple generators work without CPS closures.
acceptanceCriteria: When use_state_machines is true and function is a generator, compiler uses SM path instead of CPS
SM function takes 2 params: state machine object (slot 0) and resume value (slot 1)
All local variable access in the generator body uses OP_GET_STATE_FIELD/OP_SET_STATE_FIELD instead of OP_GET_LOCAL/OP_SET_LOCAL
Parameters are copied from the state object fields at function entry (case 0)

Each yield point: (a) writes next resume_point index to state via OP_SET_STATE_FIELD, (b) pushes yielded value, (c) emits OP_YIELD_SM or reuses OP_YIELD with modified semantics — pops only the value, no continuation
After-yield code is reachable via the dispatch table from US-006
Simple sequential generator (yield, yield, yield with no loops/ifs) produces correct values
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: This story handles the simplest case: sequential yields with no control flow. Nested if/while come in US-009/US-010.

userStories.title: Stream and OP_STREAM_NEXT support for state machine generators
userStories.description: As the VM, I need to create state machine objects for generators at call time and drive them via OP_STREAM_NEXT, so state-machine-compiled generators produce values correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: Generator call (OP_CALL on a generator closure with use_state_machines): allocates OBJ_STATE_MACHINE with field count from closure metadata, stores SM closure, copies arguments into state fields
JaclStream struct: new state_machine field (JaclVal) to hold state object reference alongside existing next_fn
OP_STREAM_NEXT: if stream has a state_machine (not nil), calls sm_closure(state_obj, resume_value) instead of calling next_fn continuation closure
First call passes JACL_NIL as resume value (no prior yield to resume from)
VM_YIELD return: stream caches yielded value, stream state = STREAM_PENDING
Normal return (VM_OK, no yield): stream state = STREAM_EXHAUSTED
terminal_k creation skipped for state machine generators
GC: Stream traces its state_machine field in gc_collect.c
Test: simple generator (no loops) yielding 3 values works end-to-end with collect
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: This wires up the runtime side. Combined with US-007, basic sequential generators should work end-to-end.

userStories.title: Yield inside while loops (state machine)
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to handle yield inside while-loop bodies in state machine mode, replacing the CPS self-referencing cell + loopback closure pattern with simple backward jumps.
acceptanceCriteria: While-loop in SM mode: emits standard backward jump (OP_LOOP) for iteration, no loopback closure
Yield inside while body: resume point dispatch jumps to the code after the yield within the loop body
After resuming, execution continues in the loop (re-evaluates condition, continues iterating)
Mutable loop counter (mut i) stored in state object field, survives across yields
Test: generator with while-loop yielding 0..N produces correct sequence via collect
Test: generator with while-loop and mut counter incrementing each iteration
CPS while-loop pattern (compiler__compile_cps_while) bypassed when use_state_machines is true
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: This is where state machines really shine vs CPS — no loopback closure, no self-referencing cell, just a backward jump.

userStories.title: Yield inside if-statements and nested control flow
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to handle yield inside if-statements and arbitrarily nested control flow in state machine mode, so generators work regardless of where yield appears.
acceptanceCriteria: Yield inside if-then branch: resume point jumps directly into the then-branch code after the yield
Yield inside if-else branch: separate resume points for then and else yields
Yield inside while-in-if: resume point reconstructs both the if-branch and loop context
Multiple yields in both branches of an if: each gets unique resume point
Test: generator with if (cond) { yield 1; yield 2 } else { yield 3 } produces [1,2] or [3] correctly
Test: generator with yield in 3 levels of nesting produces correct sequence
Test: generator with while containing if containing yield works correctly
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Control flow flattening: each yield gets a unique resume label, and the dispatch table at function entry jumps directly to the right nesting level.

userStories.title: Derived streams with state machine generators
userStories.description: As the VM, I need derived streams (filter, transform, take, lines) to work correctly when their source is a state machine generator, so stream pipelines work end-to-end.
acceptanceCriteria: vm__pull_stream_one() handles state machine generators: calls sm_closure(state_obj, resume_value) when source stream has state_machine field set
filter on SM generator: lazy filter stream pulls from SM generator correctly
transform on SM generator: lazy transform stream pulls from SM generator correctly
take on SM generator: take stream pulls N elements then stops
Chained pipeline: generator | filter | transform | collect works end-to-end
OP_COLLECT works with SM generators (inlined stream consumption loop handles SM path)
Test: SM generator piped through filter + collect produces correct subset
Test: SM generator piped through transform + collect produces correct mapped values
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: The pull helper vm__pull_stream_one already handles generator vs derived dispatch. Just need to add the SM generator case alongside the existing CPS generator case.

userStories.title: OP_AWAIT_SM opcode for state machine await
userStories.description: As the VM, I need a new OP_AWAIT_SM opcode that suspends the current state machine when awaiting a pending future, or resumes inline if the future is already resolved.
acceptanceCriteria: OP_AWAIT_SM added to OpCode enum in bytecode.c — pops future from stack, reads state object from frame stack_base + 0
If future is resolved: writes resume value to state object, calls SM function inline with (state_obj, result) — or just continues execution at next instruction
If future is pending: registers state object as a future waiter and returns VM_OK to suspend the current task
Opcode name registered in debug table
Update test/test_bytecode.c opcode enum test
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: This is the VM-side opcode. Compiler emission for await comes in the next story. Scheduler support for SM resumption comes in US-014.

userStories.title: Compiler: emit OP_AWAIT_SM for await in state machine mode
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to compile await as a state machine suspension point using OP_AWAIT_SM, so async functions use the state machine path when the flag is enabled.
acceptanceCriteria: When use_state_machines is true and a function contains await, compile as state machine (not CPS)
Each await compiles as: evaluate future expression, write next resume_point to state, emit OP_AWAIT_SM
Sequential awaits in one function: each gets its own resume point in the dispatch table
def x [await expr] pattern: resume value is stored into the appropriate state field for local x
SM function entry dispatch handles await resume points alongside yield resume points
CPS await path unchanged when use_state_machines is false
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra

userStories.title: Scheduler support for state machine resumption
userStories.description: As the runtime scheduler, I need to resume state machine functions when futures resolve, so the work-stealing scheduler can drive async state machines.
acceptanceCriteria: FutureWaiter struct extended: can hold either a continuation closure (existing) or a state machine object (new), distinguished by a tag or by checking object type
runtime__schedule_continuation updated: accepts either a closure or state machine, dispatches to appropriate task executor
New task executor runtime__state_machine_task_exec: calls sm_closure(state_obj, resume_value) on the worker's VM
Error handling in SM task exec: if SM function returns error, reads error_k from state object and schedules it with the error
runtime__schedule_waiters works with both closure and state machine waiters
Worker pinning: state machine tasks respect pinning via the SM closure's pin fields
GC roots: state machine object registered as GC root in task data
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: This enables end-to-end async SM: compiler emits OP_AWAIT_SM (US-013), VM registers SM waiter (US-012), scheduler resumes SM (this story).

userStories.title: Error propagation via error_k on state object
userStories.description: As the runtime, I need the error_k field on state machine objects to propagate errors reliably, replacing the __k upvalue[0] CPS convention.
acceptanceCriteria: error_k field set at state machine creation time: compiler emits code to store the caller's error handler
For generators: error_k is the stream's error handler (or nil if none)
For async functions: error_k is the completion future's resolver closure
runtime__state_machine_task_exec: on error, checks state->error_k, schedules it with error value
If error_k is nil, error is reported via VM error mechanism (not silently dropped)
Test: async function that throws after an await — error propagates to caller's future
Test: generator that throws after a yield — error propagates correctly
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: SM generators propagate errors through OP_COLLECT, OP_STREAM_NEXT, and vm__pull_stream_one. Error detected as VM_OK with error value on stack.

userStories.title: End-to-end async state machine tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I need comprehensive tests verifying that async functions compiled as state machines work correctly with the scheduler, including concurrent scenarios.
acceptanceCriteria: Test: function with 3 sequential awaits produces correct result with only 1 state object allocation
Test: concurrent test with multiple workers, async SM function awaiting futures, correct results
Test: async function that spawns work, awaits the future, processes the result
Test: nested async calls (SM function awaits result of another SM function)
Test: single-threaded mode: await calls SM function inline with resolved value
All tests pass with use_state_machines = true
All existing tests still pass with use_state_machines = false (CPS unchanged)
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra

userStories.title: Convert parallel join to state machine resumption
userStories.description: As the compiler and runtime, I need parallel's join continuation to use state machine resumption instead of a CPS closure, so parallel blocks don't allocate join closures.
acceptanceCriteria: Parallel bodies still compiled as separate closures (they run on different threads — unchanged)
Join point is a state machine resume point: compiler emits resume_point write before OP_PARALLEL
ParallelAgg struct: new state_machine field (JaclVal) replaces or supplements continuation field
ParallelAgg stores resume_point index for the join point
runtime__complete_parallel_slot: last completing task (atomic counter == count) resumes parent SM with results vector as resume value
Error handling: if any parallel body errors, error_k from state object is scheduled
Thread safety: unchanged — atomic completed counter ensures only one thread resumes parent SM
GC: ParallelAgg traces state_machine field in gc_collect.c
Test: parallel with 3 bodies, parent locals survive across parallel, correct after join
All existing parallel tests pass with use_state_machines = true
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra

userStories.title: Convert race join to state machine resumption
userStories.description: As the compiler and runtime, I need race's join continuation to use state machine resumption instead of a CPS closure.
acceptanceCriteria: Race bodies still compiled as separate closures (unchanged)
Join point is a state machine resume point: compiler emits resume_point write before OP_RACE
RaceAgg struct: new state_machine field replaces or supplements continuation field
RaceAgg stores resume_point index for the join point
runtime__complete_race_slot: winning task (CAS 0->1) resumes parent SM with winner result
Losing tasks silently discard (unchanged behavior)
Error handling: if winning task errors, error_k from state object is scheduled
Thread safety: unchanged — CAS-based winner selection ensures only one thread resumes parent SM
GC: RaceAgg traces state_machine field in gc_collect.c
All existing race tests pass with use_state_machines = true
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra

userStories.title: Mixed suspension: yield + await in same function
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to handle generator functions that also await futures (async generators), where both yield and await are suspension points in the same state machine.
acceptanceCriteria: Suspension analysis identifies both yield and await points in the same function, assigns sequential resume point IDs
Yield points dispatch as generator yields (VM_YIELD return)
Await points dispatch as future waits (OP_AWAIT_SM)
Same dispatch table handles both resume-from-yield and resume-from-await
Test: async generator that awaits a future then yields the result, repeated in a loop
Test: generator with interleaved yield and await produces correct sequence
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra

userStories.title: Remove CPS compilation path from compiler
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want to remove the CPS compilation path entirely now that state machines handle all suspension.
acceptanceCriteria: use_state_machines flag defaults to true (or is removed entirely)
compiler__emit_continuation deleted (~100 lines at compiler.c:1767-1873)
compiler__compile_cps_stmts and related CPS dispatch deleted (~250 lines at compiler.c:2649-2900)
compiler__compile_cps_while (self-referencing cell + loopback closure pattern) deleted
is_cps flag removed from Compiler struct
__k convention removed: no upvalue[0] error forwarding, no compiler__emit_get_k helper
suspension_map usage reviewed: keep if still used for suspension detection, remove CPS-only parts
use_state_machines field removed from Compiler struct (no longer optional)
All tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Only do this after all suspension types (yield, await, parallel, race) are verified working with state machines.

userStories.title: Remove CPS runtime support
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want to clean up runtime and VM code that only exists to support CPS continuation closures for suspension.
acceptanceCriteria: vm__make_terminal_k deleted (vm.c:657-673) — no terminal continuation closures needed
FutureWaiter struct simplified: only state machine path, closure waiter path removed
ParallelAgg.continuation closure field removed (replaced by state_machine field)
RaceAgg.continuation closure field removed (replaced by state_machine field)
runtime__continuation_task_exec simplified or removed if all resumptions go through SM executor
ContinuationTaskData struct removed if no longer used
Error recovery code in task executor simplified (no __k upvalue[0] check, just error_k field)
No dead code remaining related to CPS continuation scheduling
All tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra

userStories.title: Liveness optimization for state object fields
userStories.description: As the compiler, I want to optionally reduce state object size by only including locals that are live across at least one suspension point.
acceptanceCriteria: New analysis pass: for each local, determine if it is live (defined before, used after) across any suspension point
Locals that never cross a suspension boundary stay on the stack as normal OP_GET_LOCAL/OP_SET_LOCAL
State object only contains cross-suspension locals + parameters
Analysis is O(n) — single pass with local liveness tracking
Conservative mode (all locals in state) remains available as fallback
Test: function with 10 locals but only 2 cross a yield — state object has 2 fields plus params
All existing tests pass with optimization enabled
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Deferred optimization. Not needed for correctness — conservative mode works fine. Implement only after all other stories are done and validated.
